why: The agent list ended in a loose `\[bot\]`, and that wildcard asserted something false: that every GitHub App signing a trailer is an AI agent. Measured on 2026-08-30: `ducado` was accused of "1 of 25 commits with AI co-authorship" and the ONLY trailer in the whole history is `dependabot[bot]`; in `openkartline` the wildcard inflated the accusation from 2 to 6, because 4 of the 6 were dependabot. A dependency bumper does not write code from a prompt — it is the same judgment the `identidade-git` rule already makes with `EH_BOT`. Both sides have the SAME dependabot commit; the `fail` side adds ONE commit with AI-agent co-authorship, and that is the only difference. Whoever gives the wildcard back turns the `pass` side red; whoever removes the whole enumeration turns `fail` green.
